## Project Overview

The [NASA Turbofan RUL Forecast](nasa-rul.qmd) project develops a model to estimate the remaining useful life (RUL) of an engine from its sensor history. This companion project focuses on taking that predictive-maintenance workflow beyond offline analysis: it packages the model-serving workflow with Docker and MLflow and makes predictions available through a live HTTP API.

The service is deployed on Render. Its interactive OpenAPI documentation lets visitors inspect the request and response formats and try the available endpoints.

## How It Works

1. A client sends an engine identifier (optional) and one or more cycle records containing a cycle number and sensor readings.
2. The API uses the supplied history to produce a predicted RUL, an alert indicator, and the model version used.
3. The caller can use the prediction and alert in a downstream maintenance workflow.

## API Endpoints

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `GET /health` | Check that the service is responding. |
| `GET /model-info` | Retrieve information about the model served by the API. |
| `POST /predict` | Submit engine cycle data and receive a predicted RUL, alert status, and model version. |

The prediction endpoint validates incoming requests and documents validation errors, making the API contract visible and testable through the interactive API docs.

## What This Demonstrates

This deployment complements the model-development notebook with practical machine-learning engineering: packaging an inference service in a container, managing the model workflow with MLflow, defining a documented API contract, and deploying the service for remote access. It shows how an offline RUL model can be exposed as an integration point for applications and maintenance systems.
